full_judgment:
2. It appears that the charge sheet has been submitted against the present petitioner under section 186 of the Penal Code on the allegation that while he was in charge of the Ministry of Home Affairs he directed the then Superintendent of Police, Gopalgonj over phone to drop the name of former State Minister Kazi Firoj Rashid from the case which started on the basis of an ejhar dated 1-1-89. This allegation was made by a confidential correspondence from the then Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs. On the basis of this letter, the investigating-officer after investigation, submitted charge-sheet on 30-4-92 against other accused under different sections of the Penal Code and against the present petitioner under section 186 of the Penal Code. 

 7. Mr Mahbubur Rahman, the learned Advocate has argued that the allegation does not attract the offence of section 186 of the Penal Code. In support of his views he refers to the case of State vs Fazar Ali reported in 9 DLR 77. 

 10. Under such circumstances we are of the view that this allegation of giving instruction over telephone cannot be the basis of proceeding against the petitioner under section 186 of the Penal Code. Even if there is any statement of the Superintendent of Police to the effect that he received a telephonic call from the petitioner such evidence cannot be basis of implicating the petitioner in the case because the identity of the caller cannot be proved. So, we are of the view that the case cannot proceed against the present petitioner and continuation of the proceeding shall be abuse of the process of the Court. The case so far it relates to the present petitioner is liable to be quashed.
